Welcome to SpeedRead

SpeedRead is a Rapid Serial Visual Presentation (RSVP) reader. It flashes one word (or a small chunk) at a time at a fixed location so your eyes never have to move. With practice you can read several times faster than you do across a printed page.

You can read in two ways: RSVP (the flashing word display on the Reading tab) or Page View (a traditional document view, opened from a saved document). Both share the same playback engine and bookmarks.

Reading screen — RSVP gestures

• Tap the big play button — toggles play / pause.
• Press & hold the play button — plays only while held; releases pauses immediately. Useful for short bursts.
• Double-tap any word — drops a Quick Bookmark at the current position. The word display briefly scales up to confirm.
• Tap the ± buttons (under the play button, only while listening) — adjusts speech rate by 0.10x per tap, clamped to 0.5x – 3.0x.
• Tap the headphone FAB — switches between RSVP (visual) and Listen (TTS, voice) playback. Both share the same word position.
• Screen stays on — the display will not sleep while RSVP is actively playing, so you never need to touch the screen to keep reading.

Reading screen — landscape extras

• Tap the left half of the word area — steps one word back.
• Tap the right half of the word area — steps one word forward.
• Drag horizontally across the word area — scrubs through the document. Sensitivity is configurable (Settings → Landscape scrub sensitivity).
• The play button shrinks to a corner FAB. Pick which corner(s) it shows in via Settings → Landscape Play Button Corner.

Page View — gestures

• Single-tap on the page padding / edge — toggles the floating toolbar and page indicator. They auto-hide after a few seconds of inactivity.
• Long-press a word — marks that exact word as the RSVP continuation point. When you switch back to the Reading tab, RSVP picks up from there.
• Double-tap a word — drops a Quick Bookmark at that word. A short toast confirms.
• Swipe horizontally (Paged mode) — flips between pages.
• Drag the scrollbar (Continuous mode) — jumps anywhere in the document. The scrollbar stays visible so you can see your position at a glance.
• Play FAB (bottom-right) — starts playback in whichever mode is active. In Listen (TTS) mode it narrates aloud; in RSVP mode it plays a visual-only rolling highlight at your configured WPM. Icon: play arrow for RSVP, speaker for TTS, pause when playing either. The page indicator and a preview snippet follow the active word.
• Scroll-to-highlight FAB — appears when the active word is offscreen; tap to jump back to it.

Continuous vs. Paged

• Continuous (default) — a single long scrollable view of the whole document. Best for plain text and EPUBs.
• Paged — swipe-per-page with snap. Best for documents you want to read by visual page boundaries.
• PDFs always render as native paged bitmaps, regardless of this setting. Long-press and double-tap word gestures don\'t apply to PDF pages.
• Switch modes from Settings → Page View Appearance.

Listen mode (TTS)

• Toggle Listen mode from the Reading screen\'s headphone FAB or from Page View\'s menu. Both surfaces share one playback session, so pausing in one pauses the other.
• Speech rate — Settings slider, or the inline ± buttons on the Reading screen during playback.
• Pitch — Settings → Listening.
• Two backends:
   • System — your phone\'s built-in TTS engine. Fast to start, voice quality varies by device. Use the Language filter to narrow a long voice list down to one language.
   • Neural (Piper) — high-quality offline neural voices. Open the in-app Voice Catalog (Settings → Listening → Browse voice catalog) to download voices on demand.
• Lock screen / Bluetooth headset controls — play, pause, and skip ±10 words. The notification stays live as long as TTS is playing.
• Auto-save — your position is saved every five seconds while playing, so a closed app or background kill costs at most a few words.
• Mode memory — the app remembers whether you were last using RSVP or Listen mode and reopens in that mode on next launch.

Bookmarks

• Quick Bookmark — double-tap a word in either RSVP or Page View. The title is generated automatically: Quick Bookmark - Page N: "word".
• Manual bookmark — from the bookmark dialog (named bookmark with your title).
• Auto bookmark — created when you save a document; updated as you read.
• Find all bookmarks in the Library tab, grouped per document. Tap one to jump to that word.

Importing documents

• Files — PDF, EPUB, and TXT via the file picker.
• URL — paste an http(s) link to fetch and import the page text.
• Clipboard — paste any text directly.
• Share to SpeedRead — share text or a supported file from any app to import it.
• Saved documents live in the Library tab and remember your last position automatically.

Settings overview

• Reading Speed — base WPM (100–1000), chunk size (1–5 words per flash), font size, ORP toggle and ORP centering, dim-screen toggle, landscape play-button corner, landscape scrub sensitivity.
• Punctuation Timing — extra pause length per punctuation mark (comma, period, question mark, etc.) and at line / paragraph breaks.
• Word Length Timing — opt-in scaling of RSVP display duration by character count. Longer words linger; shorter words flash faster. Adjustable baseline word length and scaling factor.
• Theme — Light / Dark / System, with optional Material Dynamic colors on Android 12+.
• Text Color — RSVP word display color preset.
• Page View Appearance — separate Page View font size, color preset, Continuous / Paged scroll mode, and paragraph spacing toggle.
• Listening — TTS backend, language filter, voice picker, speech rate and pitch sliders, Neural voice catalog browser.
• Reset to Defaults — restores every setting to its installed value (does not delete your library or bookmarks).

What is ORP?

The Optimal Recognition Point is the letter in a word your eye most naturally fixates on (typically just left of center). Highlighting it keeps your gaze anchored at the same horizontal position as words flash by, which reduces eye movement and lets you read faster with less fatigue.

Tips for getting started

• Begin around 250 WPM and increase by 25–50 WPM as you grow comfortable.
• Use a chunk size of 1 until your reading speed plateaus, then try 2 to push further.
• Keep ORP highlighting on — it makes a big difference at higher speeds.
• If you lose your place, long-press in Page View on the last word you remember to re-anchor RSVP there.
• For long sessions, turn on Dim Surrounding Screen to reduce eye strain.
